evidence.invariant_reactions: univariant eutectic L ⇔ α-Al + Mg2Si

associative_matching_result.two_stage_llm_integration: The calculated Ni-Re phase diagram agrees poorly with the assessed experimental phase diagram. In particular, the retrograde solubility of the (Re) phase in the calculated diagram is very striking. An attempt was made to see how closely the assessed Ni-Re phase diagram could be modeled using simpler expressions for the thermodynamic functions. The excess entropies of mixing of the L, fcc, and cph phases were assumed to be zero. It was found that, even assuming that the L and cph phases are regular solutions, a simpler model reproduces the assessed diagram much better. The lattice stability parameters are the same. The calculated phase diagram is shown with solid lines. The unusual retrograde solubility of (Re) is no longer observed.

associative_matching_result.two_stage_llm_integration: In all, five isopleths were determined, three of which are along lines of constant Ni contents of 75 at.% Ni, 56 at.% Ni, and 28 at.% Ni, and two isopleths are along the Nb:V = 1:1 line and the Nb $_{55}$ Ni $_{45}$ -Ni $_{43}$ V $_{57}$ line. The isopleths are consistent with the previously published isothermal section at $1050^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and the liquidus projection diagram. The isopleths show the details of the phase equilibria between 1050 and $1400^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Some of the features observed in the various isopleths are summarized below: crosses the pseudobinary line at $1370^{\circ}\mathbf{C}$ , and passes through the liquid composition point of the four-phase reaction $(P)$ at $1345^{\circ}\mathbf{C}$ . The isopleth is through a line of $\mathrm{Nb}:\mathrm{V} = 1:1$ . The vertical plane through this line crosses the four-phase reaction at $1345^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The $\varepsilon$ phase and the liquidus line for the L + $\varepsilon$ region show temperature maxima of $\sim 1300$ and $\sim 1330^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , respectively, close to $\sim 74$ at.% Ni. The isopleth also shows that crystallization of liquid drops to a low value of $\sim 1130^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ at $\sim 61$ at.% Ni. The experimental data show the presence of two pseudobinaries in the Nb-Ni-V system: a peritectic reaction maximum $(p_1)$ , $\mathrm{L} + \alpha \leftrightarrow \mu$ , at $1370^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and a eutectic reaction $(e_2)$ , $\mathrm{L} \leftrightarrow \Gamma + \varepsilon$ , at $1220^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . On the V-poor side of the peritectic reaction $(p_1)$ the $(\mathrm{L} + \alpha + \mu)$ three-phase region, resulting from the reaction $(p_1)$ , terminates on the binary peritectic reaction $(p_2)$ of the Nb-Ni system at $1290^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . On the V-rich side, the $(\mathrm{L} + \alpha + \mu)$ region gives rise to a four-phase peritectic reaction $(P)$ , $\mathrm{L} + \alpha + \mu \leftrightarrow \Gamma$ , at $1345^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The resulting $(\mathrm{L} + \Gamma + \alpha)$ three-phase region interacts with the three-phase region $(\mathrm{L} + \alpha + \sigma)$ generated at $1280^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ $(p_3)$ in the Ni-V system to give rise to a four-phase reaction $(U_1)$ , $\mathrm{L} + \alpha \leftrightarrow \Gamma + \sigma$ , at $1270^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The three-phase region $(\mathrm{L} + \varepsilon + \Gamma)$ from the pseudobinary at $1220^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ interacts with the three-phase region $(\mathrm{L} + \mu + \Gamma)$ generated at $1345^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (four-phase reaction $P$ ) and gives a four-phase reaction $(U_{2})$ , $\mathrm{L} + \Gamma \leftrightarrow \varepsilon + \mu$ , at $1180^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , close to the Nb-Ni binary, and the resulting $(\mathrm{L} + \varepsilon + \mu)$ three-phase region terminates at the Nb-Ni binary eutectic $(e_{4})$ at $1175^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The three-phase region $(\mathrm{L} + \gamma + \varepsilon)$ arising out of the eutectic reaction $e_{1}$ (at $1282^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ ) of the Nb-Ni system and the three-phase region $(\mathrm{L} + \varepsilon + \Gamma)$ from the $1220^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ pseudobinary interacts at $1105^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to give a four-phase reaction $(U_{3})$ , $\mathrm{L} + \varepsilon \leftrightarrow \gamma + \Gamma$ . The three-phase region $(\mathrm{L} + \gamma + \sigma)$ due to the eutectic reaction $(e_{3})$ of the Ni-V system (at $1202^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ ) and the $(\mathrm{L} + \Gamma + \sigma)$ and $(\mathrm{L} + \Gamma$ +γ) three-phase regions, from the $U_{1}$ and $U_{2}$ reactions, respectively, interact at $1100^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to give a four-phase reaction $(E)$ , $\mathbf{L} \leftrightarrow \Gamma + \gamma + \sigma$ , through which the last liquid solidifies.

The shape of the $(\alpha \mathrm{Fe})$ solvus is influenced by the occurrence of the second-order ferromagnetic phase transi tion. Theoretical models for this effect are discussed by 79KO. In the Ti-Fe system, this effect is small because the Curie temperature of $(\alpha \mathrm{Fe})$ is changed very little by the addition of Ti. Thus, for the purpose of fitting the experimental data, the phase boundary could be adequately modeled as a regular solution, ignoring the magnetic phase transition. The boundaries plotted in the figure are the result of a thermodynamic calculation that matches the experimental data. The data and calculation are compared in the figure. The results of 57HEL, 59MOL, 63WAD and 66FIS agree well and are the basis for the evaluated diagram. The diagram is the result of a thermodynamic calculation. Beyond 2 at.% Ti, he reported an anomalous drop in the Curie temperature. Sample preparation and heat treatment are not described, but it is probable that the explanation for the anomaly is that the alloys beyond 2 at.% Ti were two phase. 73PAL, who made metastable single-phase alloys with up to 5 at.% Ti, reported that they verified the results of 59ARR out to 2 at.% Ti, but that they found continuous behavior of the critical temperature and no anomaly. This result is indicated in the figure. Calculation of the Phase Diagram. The diagram is the result of a thermodynamic calculation, except for several phase boundaries involving TiFe. The free energy functions have been arrived at by successive applications of least-squares fits of appropriate combinations of thermodynamic parameters to selected phase boundary data. The lattice stability parameters and initial values of the interaction parameters have been taken from 70KAU, 77KAU and 78KAU. The temperature coefficients of the $(\gamma \mathrm{Fe})$ phase have been adjusted slightly to match the transformation temperatures of pure Fe; the lattice stability parameters were not otherwise varied in the The solution phases and the C14 compound could be accurately modeled for this system. Phase boundaries on the Fe-rich side of the diagram are modeled more accurately than phase boundaries on the Ti-rich side. In both instances, the calculated and experimental boundaries agree within experimental accuracy; the Fe-rich side of the diagram is experimentally much better known. The phase equilibria involving the $C14$ compounds were accurately matched by this means. The phase equilibria involving TiFe, however, could not be reproduced using parameters that were also consistent with the thermodynamic data of 55KUB. Using the parameters, the calculated eutectic temperature is $1083^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (cf. 1080 to $1085^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ experimental), and TiFe undergoes a congruent transformation to the disordered $(\beta \mathrm{Ti})$ phase at $1313^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (cf. experimentally observed disappearance of TiFe at the peritectic temperature of $1317^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ ). The equilibrium phases of the Au-Pb system are: (1) the liquid, (L); (2) the fcc terminal solid solution, (Au), having a maximum solid solubility of Pb at about 0.11 at.%; (3) the fcc terminal solid solution, (Pb), having a maximum solid solubility of Au at about 0.2 at.%; (4) the $\mathrm{Cu}_{2}\mathrm{Mg}$ -type cubic intermetallic compound, $\mathrm{Au}_{2}\mathrm{Pb}$ , with no report of a solubility range; (5) the $\mathrm{Al}_{2}\mathrm{Cu}$ -type bct intermetallic compound, $\mathrm{AuPb}_{2}$ , with some solid solubility (not specified); and (6) the $\alpha\mathrm{V}_{3}\mathrm{S}$ -type tetragonal intermetallic compound, $\mathrm{AuPb}_{3}$ , with no reported solid solu bility. The $\mathrm{AuPb_2}$ and $\mathrm{AuPb_3}$ compounds may be unstable at low temperatures (below 8 and $99^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , respectively, according to the present thermodynamic model). These three intermetallic compounds are responsible for the phase diagram, which involves three peritectic reactions and a eutectic reaction. The invariant temperatures and compositions for these reactions are listed. The phase boundaries calculated from a thermodynamic assessment, using a model which is based mainly on the invariant points as given in the figure, are in very good agreement with the experimentally established phase boundaries. 
Liquidus. The liquidus curves of the Au-Pb system determined by Vogel from thermal observations, are generally confirmed by later investigators. However, the presence of the intermetallic compound, $\mathrm{AuPb}_3$ , was established later by Fujiki. Earlier, it was reported that the decrease of the freezing point of Au-Pb alloys with additions of Au was at the rate of $6.4^{\circ}\mathrm{C} / \mathrm{at}.\%$ Au. The liquidus in the range between 96.14 and 100 at.% Pb was measured. Seven L/[L+(Au)] liquidus points up to 18.8 at.% Pb were determined by emf measurements. Bhattacharyya and Reynolds investigated the composition range in detail, including the $\mathrm{L} + \mathrm{AuPb}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{AuPb}_3$ peritectic and $\mathrm{L} \rightarrow \mathrm{AuPb}_3 + (\mathrm{Pb})$ eutectic reactions from the cooling curves $(-0.5^{\circ}\mathrm{C} / \mathrm{min})$ of 14 alloys. Evans and Prince also determined the liquidus by thermal analysis, with heating and cooling rates of $1^{\circ}\mathrm{C} / \mathrm{min}$ . They referred to the arrest points obtained while the samples were stirred during cooling. All the results mentioned above are generally quite consistent. The L/[L+(Au)] liquidus observed is the only contradictory data, about $170^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ higher in the central part $(\sim 30$ at.% Pb) than that proposed by the other authors mentioned above. 
Present thermodynamic evaluation supports the results of the majority of the investigations. The experimental arrest points for the $\mathrm{L} / [\mathrm{L} + \mathrm{Au}_2\mathrm{Pb}]$ liquidus lie slightly above the modeled calculation. However, a calculation placing the liquidus on the data makes the $\mathrm{L} / [\mathrm{L} + (\mathrm{Au})]$ liquidus line lie substantially above the experimental data. The melting points of Au and Pb in the figure are accepted as 1064.43 and $327.502^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , respectively. 
Peritectic and Eutectic Reactions. Four invariant points, related to the $\mathrm{L} + (\mathrm{Au})\rightarrow \mathrm{Au}_2\mathrm{Pb}$ $\mathrm{L} + \mathrm{Au}_2\mathrm{Pb}\rightarrow \mathrm{AuPb}_2$ and $\mathbf{L} + \mathbf{A}\mathbf{u}\mathbf{P}\mathbf{b}_{2}\rightarrow \mathbf{A}\mathbf{u}\mathbf{P}\mathbf{b}_{3}$ peritectic reactions and the $\mathrm{L}\to \mathrm{AuPb}_3 + (\mathrm{Pb})$ eutectic reaction, were estimated. The $\mathrm{L} + (\mathrm{Au})\rightarrow \mathrm{Au}_2\mathrm{Pb}$ peritectic temperature of $434^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ has been taken, because of the large number of data points and a fairly good agreement. The invariant composition of this reaction has been estimated to be 43 at.% Pb from the $\mathrm{L} / [\mathrm{L} + (\mathrm{Au})]$ liquidus trend. The $\mathrm{L} + \mathrm{Au}_2\mathrm{Pb}\rightarrow \mathrm{AuPb}_2$ peritectic temperature values are in good agreement. An average value of $253^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ has been selected here. The invariant composition has been estimated to be 73.5 at.% Pb from the data, where the datum point at 72 at.% Pb and $252^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , designated as $\mathrm{L} / [\mathrm{L} + \mathrm{Au}_2\mathrm{Pb}]_{i}$ can be regarded as an $\mathrm{L} + \mathrm{Au}_2\mathrm{Pb}\rightarrow$ $\mathrm{AuPb_2}$ peritectic. For the $\mathrm{L} + \mathrm{AuPb_2}\rightarrow \mathrm{AuPb_3}$ peritectic temperature, $221.5^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ has been accepted. The intersection of this peritectic, horizontal with the $\mathrm{L} / [\mathrm{L} + \mathrm{AuPb_2}]$ and $\mathrm{L} / [\mathrm{L} + \mathrm{AuPb_3}]$ liquidus curves, occurs at the critical composition of 82.1 at.% Pb. The eutectic point at $212.5^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and 84.8 at.% Pb has been estimated from the data. 
Intermetallic Compounds. All three intermetallic compounds reported in the figure can be formed simultaneously from the liquid, if cooled in a centrifugal field of $1000\mathrm{g}$ . 
$\mathbf{AuPb}_{2}$ . It was concluded that the $\mathrm{AuPb}_{2}$ phase may have appreciable solid solubility on the basis of the observed changes in lattice parameters. However, no numerical values were reported, and thus, this phase is shown only as a line compound in the figure. The polymorphic transformation in $\mathrm{AuPb}_{2}$ at $211^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ could not be reproduced. 
Thermodynamic Evaluation of the Phase Diagram. The $\mathrm{L} / [\mathrm{L} + (\mathrm{Au})]$ and $\mathrm{L} / [\mathrm{L} + (\mathrm{Pb})]$ liquidus boundaries have been calculated with the thermodynamic properties derived above. The Situation 2 model shows very good agreement with the experimental data, so the assessed liquidus curves in the figure have been drawn according to the Situation 2 model calculations. This involves the entire liquidus contour in this system, including the liquidus portions pertaining to the pure components and to the intermetallic phases. 
The Situation 2 model calculation suggests the possibility that the $\mathrm{AuPb}_{2}$ phase and the $\mathrm{AuPb}_{3}$ phase may become unstable at low temperatures. According to the present approach, the decomposition temperatures on cooling (each involving a eutectoid reaction) are very sensitive to the choice of the invariant points in the phase diagram and also to the thermodynamic properties of each phase. Therefore, the decomposition temperatures, which are calculated to be 8 and $99^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , respectively, may involve rather large errors ( $\sim 100^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ ). However, the absence of the $\mathrm{AuPb}_{3}$ phase at room temperature and a sharp transition in the diffusion process behavior at $52^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , observed in a Au-Pb thin film couple, appear to be an indication of the decomposition reaction on cooling, involving the $\mathrm{AuPb}_{3}$ phase, which is tentatively placed at $52^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ in the figure. The predicted decomposition of the $\mathrm{AuPb}_{2}$ phase is not shown in the figure, because it has not been corroborated. The $\mathrm{AuPb}_{2}$ phase appears to be stable at all temperatures. The Situation 1 model calculation fails to indicate any decomposition at low temperatures for all three intermetallic compounds. 
Earlier Phase Diagram Calculations. A calculated Au-Pb phase diagram on the basis of the experimental data disagrees with the presently assessed diagram. Although the fitting of the phase boundaries was fairly successful, the evaluated $\Delta H$ of mixing for the liquid phase and the $\Delta H$ of fusion for the intermediate phases differ substantially from the experimental values (i.e., the evaluated $\Delta H$ of mixing is $16.8\mathrm{kJ / mol}$ at 78 at.% Pb, and the $\Delta H$ of $\mathrm{AuPb_2}$ formation from liquid components is $21\mathrm{kJ / mol}$ , which are substantially larger than the values indicated in the table). 
The compound free energy functions of the $\mathrm{Au}_2\mathrm{Pb}$ , $\mathrm{AuPb_2}$ and $\mathrm{AuPb_3}$ phases have been determined successively from the $\mathrm{L} + (\mathrm{Au})\rightarrow \mathrm{Au}_2\mathrm{Pb}$ $\mathrm{L} + \mathrm{Au}_2\mathrm{Pb}\rightarrow \mathrm{AuPb}_2$ and $\mathrm{L} + \mathrm{AuPb}_2\rightarrow \mathrm{AuPb}_3$ peritectic reactions and the $\mathrm{L}\rightarrow$ $\mathrm{AuPb}_{3} + (\mathrm{Pb})$ eutectic reaction, at the temperatures and compositions given in the table. The values obtained from the Situation 2 model are slightly closer to the experimental values, although the value for $\mathrm{AuPb_2}$ is still several kJ/mol too large.

associative_matching_result.two_stage_llm_integration: The anomaly in $\alpha/\gamma$ equilibrium induced by the magnetic transition was first proposed by Zener and again by Hillert and Wada. Typical examples exhibiting directly the anomaly are $\gamma$ loops of peculiar shape in the Fe-Cr, Fe-Tc, and Fe-Re systems. Since Cr, Tc, and Re are on the borders of $\alpha$ formers in the Periodic Table, it is understood that the tendency of these elements for stabilizing $\alpha$ rather than $\gamma$ is not so strong, and the Gibbs energy curves for $\alpha$ and $\gamma$ phases containing these elements are close to each other at temperatures just below the $A_{3}$ point. As a consequence, the Gibbs energy curve of the $\alpha$ phase may be raised by the excess energy due to the magnetic transition, crossing twice with that of the $\gamma$ phase, yielding an abnormal $\gamma$ loop.

associative_matching_result.two_stage_llm_integration: The calculated optimized phase diagram for the system in equilibrium with metallic Cr is shown in the figure. The figure is a projection of phase equilibria in the Cr-Al-O system through the Cr-corner to the $\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3$ -CrO join. That is, if $\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3$ and CrO are mixed in a proportion given by a point on this axis and are equilibrated with an excess of Cr, then the equilibrium phase assemblage can be read from the diagram. The calculated $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ content of the liquid in equilibrium with Cr varies from approximately $2\%$ of total Cr at high $\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3$ contents to about $7\%$ at low $\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3$ contents at liquidus temperatures. The liquid was assumed to contain only divalent and trivalent chrome. The only solid phases reported in this system are an $\mathrm{Al}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}-$ $\mathrm{Cr_2O_3}$ solid solution with the corundum structure, and $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{O}_4$ which is, however, stable over only a very restricted range of $T$ and composition. The melting point of $\mathrm{Cr_3O_4}$ in equilibrium with Cr (1668 °C), shown in the figure, is taken from the analysis of the $\mathrm{CrO - Cr_2O_3}$ system. A solid miscibility gap occurs at lower temperatures. Almost no quantitative data are available for equilibria involving the liquid phase at low oxygen pressures. Hulse reported that a mixture of $55.2\mathrm{wt.\%}$ $\mathrm{Cr_2O_3}$ , $25\mathrm{wt.\%}$ $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$ , and $19.8\mathrm{wt.\%}$ Cr started to melt at $\sim 1680^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . This point is shown in the figure. Muan reported a phase diagram for the system $\mathrm{Al_2O_3 - SiO_2 - CrO}$ in equilibrium with Cr. No description whatsoever of the experiments was given. The liquidus points shown in the figure were read from Muan's ternary diagram. Toker et al. also observed the existence of a compound, $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{O}_4$ , whose stability limits were determined, by quenching and petrographic analysis, to be 1650 and $1705^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . By the same technique, a eutectic temperature of $1665^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ was determined for the reaction $\mathrm{L} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cr} + \mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{O}_4$ , with a eutectic liquid composition very close to the CrO composition.

associative_matching_result.two_stage_llm_integration: The $\mathrm{NiTi_2 - NiZr_2}$ isopleth was also determined by investigating the Ti-TiNi-NiZr-Zr composition region in greater detail using DTA and alloys annealed at $700^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ for $125\mathrm{h}$, and it was found that at $700^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ the $\Psi$ phase exists between $\sim 21$ and 32 at.% Zr, but does not melt congruently. Since a more thorough study of the Ti-TiNi(β')-NiZr(φ)-Zr region was made and a liquidus-solidus maximum at $\sim 40$ at.% Ti, 38 at.% Ni, and 22 at.% Zr was reported, congruent melting of the $\Psi$ phase does not appear to be probable. Further study of the melting of the $\Psi$ phase in the $\mathrm{NiTi}_2(\pi')$ - $\mathrm{NiZr}_2(\xi)$ system is desirable.

associative_matching_result.two_stage_llm_integration: Details of the $\mathrm{AuCu}$ regions are shown in the figure. Detailed phase boundary determinations, including the indications of congruent transformations at $\mathrm{AuCu_3}$ and $\mathrm{AuCu}$ compositions, were made using the resistivity method. They also correctly indicated the existence of two-phase fields between the ordered and disordered phases. An additional phase, $\mathrm{Au}_2\mathrm{Cu}_3$ , proposed does not occur, as subsequent studies confirmed. Using electrical resistivity measurements supported by X-ray studies, precise boundaries for the different phase fields were defined and the congruent formation of $\mathrm{AuCu}$ and $\mathrm{AuCu}_3$ and the peritectoidal formation of $\mathrm{Au}_3\mathrm{Cu}$ were confirmed. They also confirmed that all of the order-disorder transformations in this system are of the classical Gibbsian type, with definite two-phase fields, contrary to some conflicting reports in the earlier literature. The galvanic cell studies showed definite enthalpy changes associated with the transformations $\mathrm{AuCu(I)} \rightleftarrows \mathrm{AuCu(II)}$ and $\mathrm{AuCu(II)} \rightleftarrows \mathrm{AuCu(D)}$ , thus confirming these to be first-order transformations. Detailed boundaries for the two-phase fields near the $\mathrm{AuCu}$ composition were also presented. A detailed and precise phase diagram between 40 and 60 at.% Au was reported by the X-ray method. The results are shown in the figure for comparison. The assessed diagram is primarily based on the high-temperature boundaries and on the $\mathrm{AuCu(II)} \rightleftarrows \mathrm{AuCu(I)}$ boundaries, for which no data was presented. The $\mathrm{AuCu(D)}\rightleftharpoons$ AuCu(II) transformation temperature is accepted as 410 $\pm 2^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The $\mathrm{AuCu(II)}\rightleftharpoons$ AuCu(I) temperature is accepted as $385\pm 2^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Some conflicting observations, which indicated the occurrence of the $\mathrm{AuCu(II)}$ phase in the $\mathrm{AuCu(I)}$ phase fields at lower temperatures, possibly were related to the difficulty in attaining equilibrium at these temperatures. The existence of a two-phase field between $\mathrm{AuCu}_3$ and $\mathrm{AuCu(I)}$ , from 34 to 37 at. $\%$ Au, and the associated eutectoid decomposition of the fcc solid solution was proposed. The eutectoid transformation of (Cu, Au) was confirmed and the eutectoid point was precisely determined to lie at 36 at. $\%$ Au and at $284^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The accepted phase diagram in this region is based on the aforementioned studies, as shown in the figure. The congruent and eutectoid temperatures at 390 and $284^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , respectively, and the eutectoid composition at 36 at.% Au are accepted as being the most precise. The congruent temperature at $390^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ has also been reported.

The equilibrium phases of the Fe-Rh system as shown in the assessed diagram are: (1) L, the liquid; (2) $\gamma$ , the fcc phase, which represents a complete range of solid solubility between approximately 1300 and $1394^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ ; (3) $\delta$ , the high-temperature bcc phase, with a solubility of up to 3 at. $\%$ Rh; (4) $\alpha$ , the low-temperature bcc phase; (5) $\alpha'$ , an ordered phase with CsCl structure; and (6) $\alpha''$ , a phase with an ordered CsCl structure, which forms from the $\alpha^{\prime}$ phase by a first-order ferromagnetic $\rightleftarrows$ antiferromagnetic transition. Liquidus, Solidus, and Peritectic. The equilibrium boundaries between the $\delta$ , $\gamma$ , and Liquid phases are based on the thermal analysis data of alloys between 1 and 21 at.% Rh. Their (adjusted) data are plotted in the figure. A best fit to their data, as described below, yielded a $L + \delta \rightarrow \gamma$ peritectic temperature of $1521 \pm 4^{\circ}C$ with approximate compositions of 3.9, 3.0, and 3.7 at.% Rh in the L, $\delta$ , and $\gamma$ phases, respectively; a stationary point at approximately $(1519^{\circ}C, 10$ at.% Rh), and the $\delta/\gamma$ boundaries are shown in the figure. The extension of the liquidus beyond 20 at.% Rh is based on a regular solution, a melting point of $1963^{\circ}C$ for pure Rh, and the enthalpy of melting for pure Rh. $\alpha \rightleftharpoons \gamma$ Transition. For many Fe alloys with an expanded $\gamma$ field, the $\alpha \rightleftharpoons \gamma$ transformation exhibits considerable hysteresis and has a martensitic character. This character makes the equilibrium boundaries difficult to determine, and they have not been measured for Fe-Rh. The equilibrium boundaries shown in the figure are estimated from the transformation measurements and are drawn so that the $T_{0}$ curve lies approximately midway between the $\mathbf{M}_{\mathrm{s}}$ and $\mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{s}}$ curves, and the equilibrium boundaries straddle the $T_{0}$ curve. $\alpha^{\prime}$ and $\alpha''$ Phases. There are a number of ways to represent the $\alpha^{\prime}$ and $\alpha''$ phase boundaries that are consistent with existing measurements. The representation shown in the figure closely follows previous work. The $\alpha^{\prime}$ phase near the equiatomic composition is ordered up to at least $800^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and transforms to the $\gamma$ phase near $1300^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . A 52 at.% Rh sample was well ordered after water quenching from $1000^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The ordered $\alpha'$ phase near the equiatomic composition undergoes a first-order ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic transition, $\alpha' \rightleftharpoons \alpha''$ , which is accompanied by a change in lattice parameter. The transition was extensively studied. Although most of the alloys studied have a transition temperature between 0 and $100^{\circ}C$ , the work shows that the transition temperature falls rapidly as the Rh content is decreased from the equiatomic range. Some of the available data are plotted in the figure. The $\alpha$ and $\alpha^{\prime}$ phases are ferromagnetic. The Curie temperatures for a range of alloys were measured and are shown in the figure. In addition to the ferromagnetic/paramagnetic transition, ordered alloys near the equiatomic composition undergo a first-order ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic transition. As an aid to evaluating the diagram, the thermodynamic model optimization procedure was used. For pure Fe, the thermodynamic functions as assessed were used. For pure Rh, which has only the liquid and the $\gamma$ (fcc) phases, the enthalpy of transformation and specific heats were used to construct the thermodynamic function for the liquid phase. For the interaction parameter in the $\gamma$ phase, a value was assigned based on the activity measurements and a small entropy value. The $\mathrm{L} / \gamma$ data between 6 and 21 at.% Rh could then be fitted to within $\pm 1^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ using a regular solution (one interaction parameter) for the liquid. This interaction parameter was then used to extend the $\mathrm{L} / \gamma$ boundaries to pure Rh. Some small adjustment of the calculated boundary was made because it was felt that the precision of the data was slightly better than $\pm 1^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , and the deviation between the calculated diagram and the data was not random. A similar procedure was used for the $\mathrm{L} / \delta$ and the $\delta / \gamma$ phase boundaries. The parameters used for the calculation are given in the table. associative_matching_result.two_stage_llm_integration: The assessed Mg-In phase diagram consists of: (1) the liquid phase; (2) the terminal cph (Mg) phase, with maximum solid solubility of 19.4 at.% In; (3) the fcc $\beta$ phase, extending from 23.2 to $\sim 93.5$ at.% In; (4) the terminal tetragonal (In) solid solution, with maximum solid solubility of 5 at.% Mg; and (5) six intermediate phases $(\beta_{1}, \beta_{2}, \beta_{3}, \beta^{\prime}, \beta^{\prime \prime}$ , and $\gamma^{\prime}$ ), formed from solid-state transformations. In the figure, the $\beta$ to $\beta^{\prime}$ and $\beta$ to $\beta^{\prime \prime}$ transformations are shown as first order. The temperatures of the invariant reactions, as shown in the figure, are well documented, except for those of $\beta \rightleftarrows \beta' + \beta''$ and $\beta + \beta' \rightleftarrows \beta_1$ . The assessed Mg-In phase diagram in the composition range of 0 to 20 at.% In is taken from previous work with minor adjustments. The liquidus and solidus curves of the $\beta$ phase and the (In) phase, as shown in the figure, are based on the results of previous studies. In the solid state, the phases and their boundaries are based on previous studies, adding the modifications of later work, for reasons that are discussed below. In the assessed Mg-In phase diagram, the (Mg) liquidus and solidus are taken from the more accurate tabulated data of previous work. The peritectic point, 23.2 at.% In, is taken from previous work, where it was obtained from the inter section of the peritectic horizontal, the extrapolation of the $\beta$ solidus, and the $(\mathbf{Mg}) + \beta /\beta$ boundary. In the assessed Mg-In phase diagram, the $\beta$ liquidus temperatures up to 95 at.% In are within $5^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ of those of previous studies. The $\beta$ liquidus temperatures in the composition range of 95 to 97 at.% In are taken from previous work to incorporate the peritectic reaction. The $\beta$ solidus temperatures up to 60 at.% In are within $5^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ of those of previous studies. For compositions higher than 60 at.% In, the $\beta$ solidus temperatures are within $5^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ of those of previous studies (see the table for experimental data). (In) Liquidus and Solidus. Previous studies independently reported the (In) liquidus and solidus temperatures (see the table). One study reported that the (In) liquidus and solidus terminated at $\sim 3$ at.% Mg and 5 at.% Mg, respectively, at $160 \pm 1^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ ; another study placed the terminal points of the (In) liquidus and solidus at $\sim 3.5$ at.% Mg and 6 at.% Mg at $160.2 \pm 0.1^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . These were in fair agreement. However, one study placed the composition of the $\beta$ phase of the peritectic reaction $(\beta + \mathrm{L} \rightleftharpoons (\mathrm{In}))$ at 86 at.% In, compared to 93.5 at.% In, by another study. The peritectic point of the former was not as accurate as that of the latter, because it was based on extrapolation of a line drawn through the melting point of In and only one (In) solidus temperature. Hence, in the assessed Mg-In diagram, the (In) liquidus and solidus are taken from the tabulated data of the latter study. In the assessed Mg-In phase diagram, the solid-state phase boundaries on the In-rich side are based on X-ray and thermal analyses of previous work, with the modifications suggested by later work. Because of uncertainties about the type of order of the $\beta$ to $\beta^{\prime}$ and $\beta$ to $\beta''$ transformations in this system, an alternative configuration of the $\beta, \beta^{\prime}$ , and $\beta''$ boundaries to that shown in the figure ( $\beta$ to $\beta^{\prime}$ and $\beta$ to $\beta''$ first order) is given in another figure, in which these transformations are shown principally as second order. Further investigation of this region of the diagram is needed. A previous study investigated the Mg-In system between 36.8 and 56.3 at.% In by XRD, at room temperature and at temperatures up to $350^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , and by heat capacity measurements, using an adiabatic calorimeter. No evidence of an orthorhombic phase with a long-period superlattice, as reported by earlier work, was found. Further, using the theory of previous work, it was shown that the existence of such a long-period superlattice is impossible theoretically. It was reported that $\beta$ to $\beta'$ and $\beta$ to $\beta''$ transformations go through two-phase fields of $\beta + \beta'$ and $\beta + \beta''$ or $\beta' + \beta''$ , respectively. It was suggested that the $\beta''$ field proposed by earlier work corresponded to the two-phase field between $\beta$ and $\beta''$ . Moreover, from the results of thermal analyses, it was concluded that there were two eutectoid reactions, corresponding to $\beta' \rightleftarrows \beta'' + \beta_2$ and $\beta \rightleftarrows \beta' + \beta''$ at 275 and $295^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , respectively. These results are supported by the X-ray and calorimetric investigations of other studies. A previous study investigated the Mg-In phase diagram between 15 and 35 at.% In by XRD and heat capacity measurements, to resolve the controversy on the identity of the intermediate phases in this composition range. Powder samples were annealed in evacuated $\mathrm{SiO}_2$ tubes at 150 to $350^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ for 1 to 120 days, followed by quenching. The samples were examined by the Debye-Sherrer method, using $\mathrm{CuK}_{\alpha}$ and $\mathrm{FeK}_{\alpha}$ X-ray radiation. The results confirmed the presence of the $\beta_{1}$ and $\beta_{2}$ phases, reported by earlier work, and confirmed the presence of $\mathrm{Mg}_{5}\mathrm{In}_{2}$ , reported in other studies. This phase was designated and indicated to form by a peritectoid reaction, $\beta' + \beta_{2} \rightleftharpoons \beta_{3}$ , at $210^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . These results are also in accord with the ill-defined maxima in the $\beta$ to $\beta'$ transition boundary reported by earlier work, which did not coincide with the $\mathrm{Mg}_{3}\mathrm{In}$ stoichiometry, and are in good agreement with the maximum point on $\beta$ to $\beta'$ transformation of other studies. It was reported that the $\beta_{1}$ phase at its maximum stability temperature $(337^{\circ}\mathrm{C})$ decomposes peritectoidally to $\beta + \beta'$ . Thus, contrary to the results of earlier work, it was noted that direct transition of $\beta_{1}$ to $\beta'$ does not occur. It was also found that the $\beta'$ phase decomposes eutectoidally $(\beta' \rightleftharpoons \beta_{1} + \beta_{3})$ at $202^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Because of the long annealing time employed, the supportive evidence for their X-ray data from heat capacity measurements, and the agreement of their X-ray analyses with those of other studies, the phases and boundaries reported have been adopted in the assessed Mg-In phase diagram. In the range of 60 to 85 at.% In, the existence of an ordered phase designated $\gamma'$ , based on $\mathrm{MgIn}_{3}$ , with a superlattice of the $\mathrm{Cu}_{3}\mathrm{Au}$ -type near 72 at.% In was reported. The $\gamma'$ phase was shown to form by a peritectoid reaction $(\gamma + \beta'' \rightleftharpoons \gamma')$ , at $114^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , and to have a homogeneity range extending from 69 to 75 at.% In at room temperature. These results are in accord with the intermediate phase of "MgIn₂ or MgIn₃," reported by earlier work, and the $\mathrm{Mg}_{2}\mathrm{In}_{5}$ phase, with a homogeneity range of 68 to 73 at.% In, reported by other studies. Other studies did not try to confirm the existence of $\gamma'$ phase in their X-ray analyses of this system.

The assessed Mo-V phase diagram is a simple diagram with complete miscibility in both the liquid and solid states. Early work recognized the existence of this extensive mutual solubility in the system, but a phase diagram was first proposed. This initial diagram shows mutual solubility as complete in both solid and liquid. The V melting point was extremely low $(1800^{\circ}\mathrm{C})$ because the V was only $95.5\%$ pure. With $99.4\%$ pure V, a later investigation yielded a V melting point of $1890^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ with a corresponding elevation of the solidus across the system. With the exception of a high point at $38.7\%$ V, the other six experimental solidus points of this later investigation with the more pure V can be fitted well by a straight-line relationship from the Mo melting point to the V melting point. 
The foregoing relations for the Gibbs energies of fusion and the excess partial molal Gibbs energies of the elements were combined with the ideal entropy of mixing to generate the Gibbs energies of formation for the liquid and solid phases. These equations were then used to calculate the equilibrium diagram, which has the following temperature-composition dependence, respectively, for the liquidus and solidus:

$$
\begin{array}{l} X _ {\mathrm {V}} (\mathrm {L}) = 2. 0 3 4 2 \times 1 0 ^ {- 3} (2 8 9 6 - T) - 1. 7 4 6 6 \times 1 0 ^ {- 6} (2 8 9 6 - T) ^ {2} \\ + 1. 2 0 7 0 7 \times 1 0 ^ {- 9} (2 8 9 6 - T) ^ {3} \\ \end{array}
$$

$$
\begin{array}{l} X _ {\mathrm {V}} (\mathrm {b c c}) = 1. 5 6 3 7 \times 1 0 ^ {- 3} (2 8 9 6 - T) - 1. 3 0 5 2 \times 1 0 ^ {- 6} (2 8 9 6 - T) ^ {2} \\ + 1. 5 1 3 4 \times 1 0 ^ {- 9} (2 8 9 6 - T) ^ {3} \\ \end{array}
$$

where $T$ is in K. The calculated diagram is nearly ideal. 
Subsequent studies of both binary Mo-V and ternary Mo-V-X alloys provided corroboration of the complete miscibility in the system. Data from the solidus was combined with thermodynamic data and with estimates of the excess partial molal Gibbs energies for both solid and liquid to calculate a diagram. Complete miscibility in both liquid and solidus states is reported.

associative_matching_result.two_stage_llm_integration: The R-(Cu, Ag)-Ge ternary systems, where R is Sc, Y, or one of the lanthanides, generally show several intermediate ternary compounds. For some of them the crystal structures have been identified: these have been reported in the tables. Similar stoichiometries and crystal structures are often formed in the two series and with the different Rs. For a few more phases, moreover, only some indication of the stoichiometry has been given in literature: all the phases known are shown in the isothermal sections presented in the figure. For a certain number of R-(Cu,Ag)-Ge systems, other phases have been described, but these were not observed in all the systems, probably due to partial investigation. (See the stoichiometries reported in the figure and compare them with the data collected in the tables.) The R-Cu-Ge isothermal sections of the alloys with $\mathbf{R} =$ Sc, Ce, Nd, Eu, Tb, and Yb have been studied, and these are shown in the figure. associative_matching_result.two_stage_llm_integration: The Cu-Cr and Cu-Nb phase diagrams are very alike. Cooling curves have been obtained for Cu-Cr alloys. By investigations on solidified microstructure of all samples, droplet-shaped morphology was never observed, indicating there is no liquid phase separation under the present experimental conditions. Therefore, the equilibrium phase diagram having an S-shaped appearance of the liquidus is verified. Regarding measurements of the liquidus temperatures, previous work is usually limited to the Cu-rich side in which a general agreement could be reached between various experiments and calculations. At the same time, a narrow liquid miscibility gap from 50 to $78\mathrm{wt}\%$ Cr was claimed, which is considered to be unacceptable. Nonetheless, the measured $T_{L}$ was also higher than the calculated one for the Cr-rich side, as shown in the figure (small triangles). In this regard, the difference between experiments and calculations in the liquidus for compositions above $30\mathrm{wt}\%$ Cr remains to be reconciled.

associative_matching_result.two_stage_llm_integration: The condensed phases in the Cr-Te system are: (1) liquid with a probable miscibility gap; (2) solid phase, bcc $(\mathrm{Cr})$ ; (3) solid phase, hexagonal $(\mathrm{Te})$ ; (4) NiAs-like intermediate phases between 52.4 and 62.0 at.% Te; and (5) at least one polytelluride phase, $\mathrm{CrTe}_3$ (monoclinic), between 70 and 75 at.% Te. In the assessed results, the NiAs-like phases are divided into high-, intermediate-, and low-temperature regions. The high-temperature region containing only the disordered $\mathrm{Cr}_{1 - x}\mathrm{Te}$ phase is speculative. At intermediate temperatures, the phase field is separated into $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -h (hexagonal-monoclinic), $\mathrm{Cr}_5\mathrm{Te}_8$ -m (monoclinic), and $\mathrm{Cr}_5\mathrm{Te}_8$ -tr (trigonal). At low temperatures, the phases are $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -l (monoclinic), $\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{Te}_3$ (trigonal), $\mathrm{Cr}_5\mathrm{Te}_8$ -m (monoclinic), and $\mathrm{Cr}_5\mathrm{Te}_8$ -tr (trigonal). An enlargement of important features of this speculative diagram is shown in the figure. The supposed solidus and the liquidus show a gap of $\sim 30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ at the maximum. This is an experimental fact but violates the phase rule unless there are two congruent transformations and two-phase fields, such as shown in the figure. An order-disorder type transition from $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -h to $\mathrm{Cr}_{1 - x}\mathrm{Te}$ at $1252^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ has been constructed to accommodate this fact, but this seems inconsistent with invariant reactions at three temperatures. The features of the diagram include an invariant eutectoid reaction at $1204^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , congruent transition points at $1283^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (melting) and $1252^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ at 55 at.% Te, as well as an assumed eutectoid reaction at $450^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ ; these are shown in enlarged form in the figure. Some peculiar features of the DTA curves lend support to this construction, which the calorimetric enthalpy increment data do not corroborate. This designation is given in the present work to the highly disordered NiAs structure speculated to form by an order-disorder reaction from $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -h beginning near $1252^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and 55 at.% Te. On the Cr-rich side, it extends to 52.4 at.% Te and forms by a metatectic reaction between (Cr) and liquid. At $1204^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and at 52.2 at.% Te it is believed to form from liquid plus $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -h. On the Te-rich side, the disordered structure starts ordering somewhere above $800^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ giving rise to the monoclinic and trigonal modifications, again with transformations believed to be higher order. This phase was reported to have a broad homogeneity range from the XRD of quenched samples: 50 to 60 at. $\%$ Te, 50 to 70 at. $\%$ Te, 50 to 66.7 at. $\%$ Te, and 52 to 61 at. $\%$ Te. The range is 50 to 65 at. $\%$ Te from metallography. A hexagonal structure is obtained by quenching the equiatomic composition from above $800^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. It is found at 53.3 at. $\%$ Te by quenching from $700^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $1000^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and in samples containing up to 54 at. $\%$ Te, when quenched from 900 and $1100^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. This phase was found in pure form between 52.4 and 53.4 at. $\%$ Te on quenching from $1150^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , whereas a trigonal distortion was found by quenching the most Cr-rich composition $\mathrm{Cr}_{0.9}\mathrm{Te}$ (52.6 at. $\%$ Te) from the same temperature. The Te-rich limit of the hexagonal structure is represented as a vertical dotted line at 53.5 at. $\%$ Te. Beyond this composition the structure is monoclinic. Monoclinic $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ was characterized as having a $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{S}_4$ -type structure. The diffraction patterns of monoclinic $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ , quenched and slowly cooled from high temperature, are very similar except in the 002 reflection, which was found in the latter and not in the former pattern. The high-temperature form is designated $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -h and is produced by the eutectoid reaction of Cr and $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -l at $574~^\circ \mathrm{C}$ and 55.5 at.% Te. At the stoichiometric composition, a $\lambda$ -type transition was observed at $630^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ in $C_p$ measurements by calorimetry. The transition temperature was $635^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ in DTA. In the diagrams, the calorimetric temperature was chosen. Thus the phase relationship between $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -l and $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -h is based only on thermal effects with no structural evidence. XRD at high temperature ( $\sim 700^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ ) showing $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -h as hexagonal between 53 and 60 at.% Te cannot be given much weight because the results are of poor quality. Also, it is not reasonable that the hexagonal structure can be quenched so easily up to 53.4 at.% Te but not beyond this composition. The monoclinic $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -h continues up to 59.2 at.% Te at $800^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. No two-phase region between the hexagonal and monoclinic structures of $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -h is detectable on the Cr-rich side; on the Te-rich side, there is only a hint of a two-phase region, $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -h + $\mathrm{Cr}_5\mathrm{Te}_8$ -m from the variation in lattice parameters between 59.2 and 59.6 at.% Te, and from the isopiestic measurements. The Cr-rich phase boundary for $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -l in the temperature interval 300 to $500^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ was given as 55.5 at.% Te and at $577^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ as 52 at.% Te from emf measurement. In the assessed diagram the Cr-rich phase boundary for $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -l is temperature independent below $574^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and is located at 56.4 at.% Te. The Te-rich phase boundary of $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -l is 59.2 at.% Te at $400^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and 59.1 at.% Te at $500^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. In the figure, $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -h on the Te-rich side, is hypothesized to decompose by a eutectoid reaction between $\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{Te}_3$ and $\mathrm{Cr}_5\mathrm{Te}_8$ -m at $450^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and 60.2 at.% Te. This has shifted the Te-rich boundary at $800^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ of $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -h from 59.2 to 59.8 at.% Te and the Cr-rich boundary of $\mathrm{Cr}_5\mathrm{Te}_8$ -m from 59.6 to 60.2 at.% Te. A phase analysis in the composition range 60 to 60.5 at.% Te for samples annealed at $400^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ is required but not available to prove this hypothesis. The two-phase mixture $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -l + $\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{Te}_3$ , found between 59.1 and 59.7 at.% Te, however, conforms to the figure. The most Te-rich NiAs-like phase is trigonal $\mathrm{Cr}_5\mathrm{Te}_8$ ( $\mathrm{Cr}_5\mathrm{Te}_{8^{\prime}}$ ). The Te-rich boundary of this phase having a composition of 62 at. $\%$ Te in the 500 to $575^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ range, is drawn on the basis of XRD, isopiestic, and DTA results. The value of 63.6 at. $\%$ Te at $377^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ obtained from effusion-mass loss data is much higher than the assessed value. A monoclinic phase ( $\mathrm{Cr}_5\mathrm{Te}_{8^{\prime}}$ -m) is found to exist between 60.5 and 61.5 at. $\%$ Te at $400^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. At $800^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the structure of the stoichiometric composition (61.5 at. $\%$ Te) is trigonal. The composition range 61.5 to 61.7 at. $\%$ Te is assigned in the figure to a two-phase mixture of $\mathrm{Cr}_5\mathrm{Te}_{8^{\prime}}$ -m and $\mathrm{Cr}_5\mathrm{Te}_{8^{\prime}}$ -tr that has never been found. This diagram has two anomalies, namely, 1) a gap between the supposed solidus and the liquidus, and 2) a narrow two-phase region within a broad homogeneous field. To assimilate these anomalies, the existence of a highly disordered phase, redesignated as $\mathrm{Cr}_{1 - x}\mathrm{Te}$ , is imagined at high temperature. This has led to the prediction of a eutectoid decomposition of $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -h at 60.2 at.% Te at a temperature very close to $455^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Further, in the figure, a miscibility gap is assumed within $\mathrm{Cr}_5\mathrm{Te}_8$ to rule out a continuous transition from the monoclinic to the trigonal form, though it cannot be clarified at present as to how, the disordered $\mathrm{Cr}_{1 - x}\mathrm{Te}$ phase at high temperature orders itself into the monoclinic and trigonal forms of $\mathrm{Cr}_5\mathrm{Te}_8$ . The crystal structures observed in the Cr-Te system between 52 and 62 at. $\%$ Te are derived from hexagonal NiAs by ordering of vacancies in alternate metal layers. The idealized stoichiometries of ordered structures have been used to designate various phases. Thus $\mathrm{Cr_3Te_4 - h}$ and $\mathrm{Cr_3Te_4 - l}$ are assigned the same crystal structure. No single crystal data is available for $\mathrm{Cr_5Te_8 - m}$ and $\mathrm{Cr_5Te_8 - tr}$ , in which the ordered arrangements of Cr atoms in partially vacant layers are virtually identical. In $\mathrm{Cr_5Te_8 - m}$ the stacking of these layers is such that the Cr atoms occupy alternating positions when projected along $c$ , whereas in $\mathrm{Cr_5Te_8 - tr}$ , Cr atoms presumably occupy positions that are coincidental. A tentative structure of $\mathrm{Cr_5Te_8 - tr}$ , whose symmetry requires confirmation by single crystal work, has been proposed. This nevertheless suggests that the transition from $\mathrm{Cr_5Te_8 - m}$ to $\mathrm{Cr_5Te_8 - tr}$ cannot be continuous, as the monoclinic angle $\beta$ shows no tendency to go to $90^{\circ}$ as the Te concentration increases. Similarly, the changeover from $\mathrm{Cr_3Te_4 - h}$ , which is body-centered monoclinic, to $\mathrm{Cr_5Te_8 - m}$ , which is face-centered monoclinic, is also abrupt. In contrast, the variation of lattice parameters with composition is continuous in going from hexagonal to monoclinic in $\mathrm{Cr_3Te_4 - h}$. Lattice parameters of another ordered structure, derived from $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ with half of its vacant sites occupied by Cr atoms and an ideal stoichiometry of $\mathrm{Cr}_7\mathrm{Te}_8$ were given. But there are many contradictions: 1) Monoclinic $\mathrm{Cr}_7\mathrm{Te}_8$ was obtained by quenching the stoichiometric composition from $700^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, whereas an equiatomic composition quenched from the same temperature gave hexagonal $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -h. In both samples free Cr coexisted. Had $\mathrm{Cr}_7\mathrm{Te}_8$ been an equilibrium phase, it would have been found in the equiatomic sample as well. 2) Lattice parameters of $\mathrm{Cr}_7\mathrm{Te}_8$ with its face-centered monoclinic structure established from oscillation photographs, are very close to the lattice parameters given for $\mathrm{Cr}_5\mathrm{Te}_8$ with $\mathrm{Cr}_5\mathrm{Te}_6$ being shown by neutron diffraction of polycrystalline samples to have a body-centered unit cell of a partially filled $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ structure. 3) Whereas $\mathrm{Cr}_7\mathrm{Te}_8$ was found as an ordered structure (space group: Cz/c) below $400^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , it was found only above $500^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. 4) The observed decrease of the relative unit cell volume by nearly $4\%$ cannot be accounted for by the ordering of cation vacancies alone. 5) The lattice parameters of $\mathrm{Cr}_3\mathrm{Te}_4$ -h vary continuously with composition, and the angle, $\beta$ , with increasing Cr-content, rapidly approaches the value of $90^{\circ}$ at the composition where $\mathrm{Cr}_7\mathrm{Te}_8$ should have been.

However, the phase boundary for the $\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{U}$ -rich side under constrained vapor conditions has not been previously established, and the diagram shown in the figure is based on a number of investigations as described below. This figure represents the equilibrium phases and compositions under the equilibrium dissociation pressure of the hydride produced by the reaction:

$$
\mathrm {H} _ {3 - X} \mathrm {U} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm {U} (\text {s o l i d s o l u t i o n}) + \frac {3 - X}{2} \mathrm {H} _ {2}
$$

The actual melting temperature for $\mathbf{H}_3\mathbf{U}$ is not accurately known but could conceivably account for the incipient fusion indicated. Within this temperature span, the stoichiometry of uranium hydride is very close to $\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{U}$ and its activity as well as that of uranium may be considered as unity in the equilibrium mixture. Consequently, we can write:

$$
\begin{array}{l} \Delta G ^ {0} \left(\mathrm {H} _ {3} \mathrm {U}\right) = R T \ln \frac {a _ {\mathrm {U}} a _ {\mathrm {H} _ {2}} ^ {3 / 2}}{a _ {\mathrm {U H} _ {3}}} = \frac {3}{2} R T \ln P _ {\mathrm {H} _ {2}} \\ = - 3 0 5 0 0 + 4 3. 3 8 T = - 1 7 5 6 6 \quad (2 9 8 K) \\ \end{array}
$$

where $a_{i}$ is the activity of component $i$ and $T$ is temperature in Kelvin. The agreement is excellent. However, the former leads to a hydrogen pressure of 1 atm at $696.2\mathrm{K}$ $(423.1^{\circ}\mathrm{C})$ , while the latter yields a temperature of $703.1\mathrm{K}$ $(430^{\circ}\mathrm{C})$ . The latter is in better agreement with the value of $432 \pm 3^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The value of $430^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ is the mean obtained. Therefore, this is the preferred relation. With the known enthalpy and entropy for the transformations of uranium and neglecting $\Delta C_p$ we have:

$$
\begin{array}{l} \mathrm {U} (\alpha) \rightarrow \mathrm {U} (\beta) \quad \Delta G ^ {0} = 6 6 7 - 0. 7 0 8 T \\ U (\beta) \rightarrow U (\gamma) \quad \Delta G ^ {0} = 1 1 3 7 - 1. 0 8 4 T \\ \end{array}
$$

we can write:

$$
\begin{array}{l} \begin{array}{l}\mathrm {U} (\alpha) + 3 / 2 \mathrm {H} _ {2} \rightarrow \mathrm {H} _ {3} \mathrm {U} (\beta)\\\Delta G ^ {0} = - 3 0 5 0 0 + 4 3. 3 8 T\end{array}\quad (2 9 8 - 9 4 2 \mathrm {K}) \\ \begin{array}{l}\mathrm {U} (\beta) + 3 / 2 \mathrm {H} _ {2} \rightarrow \mathrm {H} _ {3} \mathrm {U} (\beta)\\\Delta G ^ {0} = - 3 1 1 6 7 + 4 4. 0 8 8 T \quad (9 4 2 - 1 0 4 9 \mathrm {K})\\\end{array} \\ \begin{array}{c}\mathrm {U} (\gamma) + 3 / 2 \mathrm {H} _ {2} \rightarrow \mathrm {H} _ {3} \mathrm {U} (\beta)\\\Delta G ^ {0} = - 3 2 3 0 4 + 4 5. 1 7 2 T\end{array} \\ \end{array}
$$

The concentrations in both the U-rich and $\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{U}$ -rich phases must be described in terms of $X_{\mathrm{U}} + X_{\mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{U}} = 1$ . At $660^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (933 K), $X_{\mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{U}} = 0.937$ , and the concentration of uranium in the uranium-rich phase (employing Sievert's law with $\mathbf{K} = 2.2$ ppm to obtain $\% \mathrm{H}$ ) is 99.87 wt.% U or $X_{\mathrm{U}(\alpha)} = 0.999$ . Therefore, we have $X_{\mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{U}} / X_{\mathrm{U}} = 0.938$ . Substituting the equations and solving for the activity ratio yields 0.884. These results imply that the corresponding activity coefficient ratio is 0.942, a reasonable result. Similarly, at $1120^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (1393 K), substituting the equations yields 0.423 for the activity ratio $a_{\mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{U}} / a_{\mathrm{U}}$ , whereas $X_{\mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{U}} / X_{\mathrm{U}} = 0.742 / 0.959 = 0.77$ , and therefore, $\gamma_{\mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{U}} / \gamma_{\mathrm{U}(\gamma)} = 0.55$ . 
However, their data for higher temperatures showed a very rapid increase of the solubility of uranium in the hydride phase and their values of $-\ln X_{\mathrm{U}}$ fall far below the range indicated on the figure and were not plotted. The reason for the gross discrepancy in these data with the data of other investigators is not known. 
It should not be construed that these results confirm the phase diagram but only that they are not grossly inconsistent. Thermal analysis of alloys with compositions in the two-phase regions at equilibrium hydrogen pressures would be very helpful in confirming the isotherms and in yielding additional evidence for the partial or incipient fusion of $\mathrm{H}_{3 - X}\mathrm{U}$ at $1050^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Work indicates that $\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{U}$ melts in the range 1005 to $1085^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ at a pressure of 578 atm (8500 psi). If partial fusion occurs at $1050^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ leading to equilibrium between a liquid phase, $\mathrm{H}_{3 - X}\mathrm{U}$ , uranium solid solution and hydrogen, then this would require an isotherm terminating in a peritectic or eutectic reaction near the $\mathrm{H}_{3 - X}\mathrm{U}$ phase boundary. associative_matching_result.two_stage_llm_integration: It was reported earlier that three solid phases take part in the phase equilibria in the Ti-rich region of the Ti-Si-Ga system (below 38 at.% Ga and above 62 at.% Ti) at $1350^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . These phases are the $\beta$ Ti solid solution ( $\beta$ ), the compound $\mathrm{Ti}_5\mathrm{Si}_3$ with Ga in solid solution denoted as $\mathrm{Ti}_5(\mathrm{Si},\mathrm{Ga})_3$ , or z in this article and the compound $\mathrm{Ti}_2\mathrm{Ga}$ designated as $\chi$ . The same phases were found in the as-cast alloys. Therefore, these phases are involved in the solidification processes. Data on the constitution of the as-cast samples and those annealed at $1350^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ are listed in the tables. These data, which were obtained by means of metallography, XRD, EPMA, and DTA techniques, are considered in more detail below. They were used to construct the Ti-Si-Ga phase diagram presented as the solidus surface projection. The homogeneity range of the $\beta$ solid solutions was found to extend along the Ti-Ga side of the ternary Ti-Si-Ga phase diagram in accord with the high Ga solubility in $\beta \mathrm{Ti}$ in the binary Ti-Ga system (up to 27 at.% Ga at $1420^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ ). The maximum Si solubility in $(\beta \mathrm{Ti})$ is accepted to be 4.7 at.% in the binary Ti-Si system at $1355^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . It decreases with increasing Ga content and changes insignificantly with lowering of temperature as shown by EPMA. It should be noted that the $\beta$ phase with the bcc W-type structure was never observed during this investigation, because the high-temperature $\beta$ phase disappeared during cooling to room temperature after undergoing a number of phase transformations depending on composition. Thermal effects at $\sim 900$ to $925^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ corresponding to the $\alpha \leftrightarrow \beta$ transformation were observed on the DTA curves during both heating and cooling. Precipitation of $\mathrm{Ti}_{2}\mathrm{Ga}$ as a result of decreasing Ga solubility with decreasing temperature was shown to occur by microstructural analysis (MSA) and XRD for those alloys that contained $\beta$ phase with more than $\sim 18$ at.% Ga. The lattice parameters of the $\alpha$ phase, formed as a result of the phase transformations of the $\beta$ phase, decrease with increasing Ga content owing to the substitution of smaller Ga atoms for larger Ti atoms. Solution of Si in Ti shows a similar effect. Besides the thermal effect resulting from the $\alpha \rightarrow \beta$ transformation, the DTA curves for the as-cast alloys containing a Ga-rich Ti phase were found to show an additional thermal effect at 1000 to $1035^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ due to the occurrence of the $\mathrm{Ti}_3\mathrm{Ga}(\alpha_2)$ phase. This last effect was not observed for those alloys annealed at $1350^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The phase equilibria observed at $1350^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and reported recently apply up to the solidus temperatures. The solidus surface projection is shown in the figure. The phase equilibria in the region of investigation are characterized by the absence of any ternary compounds and involve only the pseudobinary phases. The $\mathrm{Ti}_{5}(\mathrm{Si},\mathrm{Ga})_{3}(\mathrm{z})$ is a phase based on the $\mathrm{Ti}_{5}\mathrm{Si}_{3}$ binary compound. It extends up to $\sim 25$ at.% Ga and coexists with the Ti-Ga-base phases ( $\beta$ , $\mathrm{Ti}_{2}\mathrm{Ga}(\chi)$ , $\mathrm{Ti}_{5}\mathrm{Ga}_{3}(\mathrm{g}))$ . It forms an extended ( $\beta + \mathrm{Ti}_{5}(\mathrm{Si},\mathrm{Ga})_{3}$ ) two-phase field, a ( $\mathrm{Ti}_{2}\mathrm{Ga} + \mathrm{Ti}_{5}(\mathrm{Si},\mathrm{Ga})_{3}$ ) narrow two-phase field, and two three-phase regions: ( $\mathrm{Ti}_{5}(\mathrm{Si},\mathrm{Ga})_{3} + \mathrm{Ti}_{2}\mathrm{Ga} + \mathrm{Ti}_{5}\mathrm{Ga}_{3}$ ) and ( $\beta + \mathrm{Ti}_{5}(\mathrm{Si},\mathrm{Ga})_{3} + \mathrm{Ti}_{2}\mathrm{Ga}$ ). With the aim of defining the $\mathrm{Ti}_{5}(\mathrm{Si},\mathrm{Ga})_{3}$ apex of the $(\beta + \mathrm{Ti}_{5}(\mathrm{Si},\mathrm{Ga})_{3} + \mathrm{Ti}_{2}\mathrm{Ga})$ tie-triangle, an additional experiment was carried out. In the as-cast eutectic alloys 75Ti-5Si-20Ga and 75Ti-3Si-22Ga, the $\mathrm{Ti}_{5}(\mathrm{Si},\mathrm{Ga})_{3}$ phase is present only or almost only as very fine particles in a eutectic matrix, and they grow during annealing. The $\mathrm{Ti}_{5}(\mathrm{Si},\mathrm{Ga})_{3}$ grains formed during annealing are at equilibrium, whereas the large grains of the primary crystallized silicide phase do not reach an equilibrium state even during a long annealing time. The additional EPMA investigation of these alloys provides more reliable data concerning the position of the apex point of $\mathrm{Ti}_{5}(\mathrm{Si},\mathrm{Ga})_{3}$ of the tie-triangle.

associative_matching_result.two_stage_llm_integration: We have attempted a theoretical calculation of the phase boundaries in the Pu-Ta system by utilizing the Miedema model to estimate the enthalpies of formation in the liquid and in the solid (bcc) phases, and assuming ideal entropy of mixing in both phases. The phase diagram obtained on using the theoretical values of enthalpies of formation is shown in the figure. Calculation of the phase boundaries at and below the melting point of Pu reveals greater solubility of Ta in (εPu) than in liquid Pu thus suggesting that the Pu-Ta system is actually of a simple peritectic type (akin to the U-Ta system). However, the liquidus trend calculated using the values for the enthalpies of formation obtained from the Miedema model turned out to be slightly displaced towards higher Ta content when compared with the experimental data. Hence, the values for the enthalpies of formation obtained from the Miedema model were adjusted to fit the liquidus data. In addition, invariant reactions may be expected in connection with each of the allotropic transformations of $\mathbf{Pu}$ . The calculations also suggest a pronounced retrograde solidus for the (Ta) phase. The invariant reactions below $400^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ have not been modeled. The peritectic reaction and the eutectoid reaction temperatures are $679^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $471^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , respectively. The phase diagram calculated using the Miedema model, combined with the ideal entropy of mixing, appears to be a very good approximation of the experimental phase boundaries in the Pu-Ta system. It was necessary to adjust the values of the enthalpy of formation because an estimate of the magnitude of the excess entropy of mixing was not possible without making assumptions regarding the (Ta) solidus.

associative_matching_result.two_stage_llm_integration: The assessed Mg-In phase diagram consists of: (1) the liquid phase; (2) the terminal cph (Mg) phase, with maximum solid solubility of 19.4 at.% In; (3) the fcc $\beta$ phase, extending from 23.2 to $\sim 93.5$ at.% In; (4) the terminal tetragonal (In) solid solution, with maximum solid solubility of 5 at.% Mg; and (5) six intermediate phases $(\beta_{1}, \beta_{2}, \beta_{3}, \beta^{\prime}, \beta^{\prime \prime}$ , and $\gamma^{\prime}$ ), formed from solid-state transformations. In the figure, the $\beta$ to $\beta^{\prime}$ and $\beta$ to $\beta^{\prime \prime}$ transformations are shown as first order. The temperatures of the invariant reactions, as shown in the figure, are well documented, except for those of $\beta \rightleftarrows \beta' + \beta''$ and $\beta + \beta' \rightleftarrows \beta_1$ . The assessed Mg-In phase diagram in the composition range of 0 to 20 at.% In is taken from previous work, with minor adjustments. In the solid state, the phases and their boundaries are based on previous works, adding the modifications of later works, for reasons that are discussed below. Previous work investigated the Mg-In system between 36.8 and 56.3 at.% In by XRD, at room temperature and at temperatures up to $350^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , and by heat capacity measurements, using an adiabatic calorimeter. No evidence of an orthorhombic phase with a long-period superlattice, as reported previously, was found. Further, using the theory, it was shown that the existence of such a long-period superlattice is impossible theoretically. It was reported that $\beta$ to $\beta'$ and $\beta$ to $\beta''$ transformations go through two-phase fields of $\beta + \beta'$ and $\beta + \beta''$ or $\beta' + \beta''$ , respectively. It was suggested that the $\beta''$ field proposed previously corresponded to the two-phase field between $\beta$ and $\beta''$ . Moreover, from the results of thermal analyses, it was concluded that there were two eutectoid reactions, corresponding to $\beta' \rightleftharpoons \beta'' + \beta_2$ and $\beta \rightleftharpoons \beta' + \beta''$ at 275 and $295^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , respectively. (See the enlarged section of the assessed Mg-In phase diagram.) These results are supported by the X-ray and calorimetric investigations of previous works. Previous work studied the Mg-In phase diagram between 15 and 35 at.% In by XRD and heat capacity measurements, to resolve the controversy on the identity of the intermediate phases in this composition range. Powder samples were annealed in evacuated $\mathrm{SiO}_2$ tubes at 150 to $350^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ for 1 to 120 days, followed by quenching. The samples were examined by the Debye-Sherrer method, using $\mathrm{CuK}_{\alpha}$ and $\mathrm{FeK}_{\alpha}$ X-ray radiation. The results confirmed the presence of the $\beta_{1}$ and $\beta_{2}$ phases, reported previously, and confirmed the presence of $\mathrm{Mg}_{5}\mathrm{In}_{2}$ , reported in other works. This phase was designated and indicated to form by a peritectoid reaction, $\beta' + \beta_{2} \rightleftharpoons \beta_{3}$ , at $210^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . These results are also in accord with the ill-defined maxima in the $\beta$ to $\beta'$ transition boundary reported previously, which did not coincide with the $\mathrm{Mg}_{3}\mathrm{In}$ stoichiometry, and are in good agreement with the maximum point on $\beta$ to $\beta'$ transformation of other works. Thus, contrary to previous results, it was noted that direct transition of $\beta_{1}$ to $\beta'$ does not occur. It was also found that the $\beta'$ phase decomposes eutectoidally $(\beta' \rightleftharpoons \beta_{1} + \beta_{3})$ at $202^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . associative_matching_result.two_stage_llm_integration: Starting from the well-characterized phase equilibria at $600^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , DTA were performed on all samples of series II. With the selected heating/cooling rate of $2\mathrm{K / min}$ it was not possible to establish the equilibrium phase composition on cooling after the first melting. Therefore, it was not useful to cycle the samples over the respective temperature range several times. Instead, in order to test for the reproducibility of the results, two or three portions of each sample were studied separately by DTA. The corresponding thermal effects are listed together with the phase compositions of the samples at $600^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The results of the DTA experiments are also shown for the four vertical sections at 66.7, 70, 75, and 85 at.% Sb. In two of the samples, the thermal effect that corresponds to the peritectic reaction P1 (indicated by (f)), appeared at remarkably higher temperatures than in the other samples. This may be due to bad thermal contact between the partly molten sample and the quartz crucible. However, when these samples were reannealed and measured again the peritectic effect appeared at the expected temperature as indicated by a solid circle $(\bullet)$ . Combining the isothermal section with the information from the DTA experiments, a complete reaction scheme was constructed for the Sb-rich part of the phase diagram. This so-called Scheil diagram involves four invariant reactions, all of them in the narrow temperature range between 615 and $642^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ : the peritectic decomposition of the ternary $\eta$ -phase, two invariant phase equilibria of the class II, and one degenerated ternary eutectic. A detailed compilation of the invariant reactions, including the compositions of the involved phases, is shown. Some interesting details were found during the construction of the phase diagram. The melting temperature of $\varepsilon$ appears to be nearly constant up to a Ni content of $\sim 10$ at.%, which also yields a rather surprising shape of the three-phase region $[\varepsilon +\delta +\mathrm{L}]$ . Additionally, the liquidus surface appears to be remarkably asymmetric: along isopleths with constant Sb content the liquidus temperatures remain almost constant in the Fe-rich part before they increase rapidly at higher Ni contents. Especially at higher Sb contents this results in a concave shape of the liquidus surface. This asymmetric form of the liquidus surface is possibly interesting from an energetic point of view, but some thermodynamic data for liquid Fe-Ni-Sb alloys would be required for further considerations.

associative_matching_result.two_stage_llm_integration: Several authors have investigated the entire composition range of the Bi-Hg system using thermal analyses, and there is qualitative agreement among their data. This report is dubious because no subsequent investigation has identified any intermediate phase in this system. Data for dilute amalgams are shown in the figure, and the majority of the more precise determinations confirm the selected results. The liquidus values for dilute amalgams, although good fits to the calculated liquidus, are given little importance because the authors presented no convincing evidence of their correctness. Because $\mathrm{AlRe}$ was observed in alloys annealed at $1273\mathrm{K}$ but not at $1373\mathrm{K}$ , a peritectoid reaction, $\mathrm{Al}_{11}\mathrm{Re}_4 + \mathrm{AlRe}_2 = \mathrm{AlRe}$ , was placed between 1272 and $1373\mathrm{K}$ , instead of the melting of $\mathrm{AlRe}$ at $1863\mathrm{K}$ . The decomposition temperature of $\mathrm{Al}_{11}\mathrm{Re}_4$ was placed at $1863\mathrm{K}$ , which was the decomposition temperature of $\mathrm{AlRe}$ . Because the $\mathrm{Al}_4\mathrm{Re}$ phase was found to exist above $1273\mathrm{K}$ , its decomposition temperature was placed at $1758\mathrm{K}$ , which was the decomposition temperature of $\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{Re}$ (now $\mathrm{Al}_{11}\mathrm{Re}_4$ ). Compared to the previous phase diagram, the phase diagram given in the figure has the liquidus compositions at much higher Re contents, so that they are not consistent with the experimental data. For example, as shown in the figure, the composition of the liquid phase at the invariant reaction $\mathrm{L} + \mathrm{Al}_{11}\mathrm{Re}_4 = \mathrm{Al}_4\mathrm{Re}$ is about 15 at.% Re, in contrast to 2.5 at.% Re (15 wt.% Re) shown in the previous phase diagram. No reason was provided for the adjustment. In the judgment of the present authors, it is likely that a mistake was made when changing the compositional axis from the weight to atomic percent of Re. The original phase diagram was in weight percent while that in the figure was in atomic percent of Re. At the Al-rich side of the system, neither the proposed peritectic reaction at $963 \pm 7\mathrm{K}$ nor the eutectic reaction at $873\mathrm{K}$ involving the fcc and liquid is plausible. The invariant temperature must be very close (within $\pm 5\mathrm{K}$ ) to the melting point of pure Al as in some other Al- $B$ ( $B$ is transition metal) systems, for example, Al-Ti and Al-V. This is due to the very low solubility of these elements in both liquid and fcc Al around the melting temperature of the pure Al. No experimental compositions are available. The four phases reported were essentially confirmed, except that AlRe was found to decompose at about $1323\mathrm{K}$ instead of melting at $1863\mathrm{K}$ . In addition, two more phases close to the Al side were found to exist, that is, $\mathrm{Al}_6\mathrm{Re}$ and $\mathrm{Al}_4\mathrm{Re}$ .

associative_matching_result.two_stage_llm_integration: Figures 1 to 3 show the assessed liquidus projection and two isothermal sections at 700 and $500^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, which are almost the same as those accepted by most reviewers except for some modifications on the liquidus projection made in this study. As shown in these diagrams, there is only one ternary intermetallic compound $\tau\mathrm{Al}_3\mathrm{Cu}_5\mathrm{Zn}_2$ in this system. The assessed liquidus projection shown in Fig. 1 is mainly based on the work of [41Kos3] and [60Arn2], following the nomenclature of [56Rhi] and the format of [79Cha]. The dashed lines are the modifications made in this study. These modifications are made so that the ternary phase equilibria are consistent with the currently accepted binary equilibria. These dashed lines are topologically correct, but should be considered tentative owing to the absence of experimental confirmation. The liquidus projection reported in earlier works [11Lev, 12Lev, 12Car, 19Jar, 20Ros, 21Hau, 25Han, 26Nis, 27Nis, 28Ham] agree only qualitatively with the investigations by [41Kos3] and [60Arn2]. The results of [41Kos2] and [60Arn2] have been widely accepted now. Only the invariant equilibria near the Al-Zn side have been determined [41Kos3] such as the invariant reactions $\Pi_1$, $\Pi_2$, and $\mathbf{I}_1$ as shown in Fig. 1. The earlier results of [19Jar] differ appreciably from those of [41Kos3]. The phase equilibria near the Curich region, especially those close to the Al-Cu binary, are not well established due to insufficient experimental data. In comparison, the isothermal curves shown in Fig. 1 and the corresponding solidus, determined by a series of investigations [41Kos1, 41Kos2, 41Kos3, 60Arn1, 60Arn2], are believed to be more reliable. The ternary solubility of the $\gamma^0$ phase, which in fact is still unknown, is modeled in this study in order to fit its stable temperature range as shown in the liquidus projection in Fig. 1. The calculated liquidus projection shown in Fig. 8 is next compared with the assessed one in Fig. 1. Although the general features of the calculated liquidus projection are in accord with those of the assessed one, there are discrepancies between the calculated temperatures and compositions of the liquid and the experimental data for the invariant reactions $\Pi_1, \Pi_2, \Pi_3, \Pi_4, \Pi_5$ and $\mathbf{I}_1$. On the basis of the composite evidence, the authors conclude that the calculated liquidus projection given in Fig. 8 as well as the calculated invariant reactions given in Table 4 could be more reliable than the assessed data given in Fig. 1 and Table 2. Until more experimental data become available, they should be used with caution.

associative_matching_result.two_stage_llm_integration: The phase diagram shown in Fig. 3 has been calculated from the expressions given in Table 9 for the Gibbs energies of transformation of pure Mg and Li and for the excess Gibbs energies, enthalpies, and excess entropies of mixing of the three phases. For purposes of comparison, Fig. 3 also shows the assessed diagram from Fig. 1. As can be seen in Fig. 3, the calculated difference in limiting slopes of the liquidus and solidus is less than the reported difference shown in Fig. 1, resulting in the calculated solidus being higher than the reported solidus.
